claims: The 14th Amendment was ratified in 1868.
The 14th Amendment grants citizenship to all born or naturalized in the US including former slaves.
The 14th Amendment prohibits states from denying due process.
The 14th Amendment guarantees equal protection under the law.
The Citizenship Clause of the 14th Amendment establishes birthright citizenship.

The Citizenship Clause of the 14th Amendment ensures that all persons born or naturalized in the United States and subject to its jurisdiction are citizens of the United States and the state they reside in.
The Privileges or Immunities Clause of the 14th Amendment prevents states from making or enforcing laws that abridge the privileges or immunities of citizens of the United States.
The Due Process Clause of the 14th Amendment prohibits state governments from depriving any person of life, liberty, or property without due process of law.
The Equal Protection Clause of the 14th Amendment requires states to provide equal protection of the law to all people within their jurisdiction.
The 14th Amendment was passed after the Civil War.
The 14th Amendment was passed to protect the rights of newly freed enslaved people.
The 14th Amendment was passed to override the Dred Scott v. Sandford decision.
The 14th Amendment extended the protections of the Bill of Rights to apply to state governments.
The 14th Amendment has been the basis for Brown v. Board of Education.
Brown v. Board of Education concerned racial discrimination.
The 14th Amendment has been the basis for Roe v. Wade.
Roe v. Wade concerned reproductive rights.
The 14th Amendment has been the basis for Bush v. Gore.
Bush v. Gore concerned election recounts.
Section 3 of the 14th Amendment prevents individuals who have engaged in insurrection or rebellion against the U.S. from holding state or federal office.
Birthright citizenship is interpreted to include children born in the U.S. of resident aliens.
The Equal Protection Clause is used to combat discrimination and ensure fair treatment for all people, including non-citizens.
The Incorporation Doctrine is used to apply the Bill of Rights to state governments.
